key_insight: ML-COHP predicts DFT-derived bond strengths from frozen MACE descriptors, reaching 0.06 eV error on relaxed grain boundaries in about a second versus 5–51 hours for LOBSTER.
engineering_relevance: Fast bond-strength estimates can support analysis of grain boundaries and catalytic nanoparticles without repeating expensive electronic-structure calculations for every geometry.
method: Extract frozen atomic descriptors from a MACE foundation model.
Use a symmetric pair head combining scalar and bond-projected vector channels.
Correct an element-embedding pair baseline to predict ICOHP.
evidence_signal: Across high-entropy diborides, Pt clusters on defective graphene, and oxygen-covered Pt/Pd nanoparticles, reported errors for bonds stronger than 0.5 eV were 1.6–4.1%, about half those of a Gaussian-process comparator trained on the same data.
watch_item: Transferability beyond the tested chemistries and geometries remains unestablished; predictions also depend on the quality of input structures.
paper_title: ML-COHP: predicting bond descriptors using latent space of a universal interatomic potentials
